source.title: Super-convergence: very fast training of neural networks using large learning rates

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, including supplemental material.
record.tranche_reason: It tests how batch size and dropout relate to test performance and the training–test gap, using its own training comparisons rather than the versions' original procedures.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports optimizer comparisons and learning-rate/Hessian estimates. Those do not test the mapped adaptive-optimizer comparison or magnitude-aware perturbation measure. Cited results from other work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The dropout comparison tests V6 using held-out accuracy. The batch-size comparisons hold iterations, rather than epochs, fixed, so they cannot establish V5's fixed-epoch effect.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that large cyclical learning rates enable much faster training and higher final test accuracy when other regularization is reduced appropriately. They also report greater benefits with limited labeled data and approximately equivalent training–test accuracy gaps for small and large batches.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies cyclical learning rates and super-convergence, rather than the original interventions or measures in the mapped claim versions. It uses its own batch-size and dropout comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size changes final test accuracy in Table 7; the paper reports that the generalization gap remains approximately equivalent across small and large batch sizes. Dropout at ratio 0.2 yields a small improvement in the reported experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: Small and large batches have approximately equivalent training–test accuracy gaps during super-convergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the tested super-convergence schedule, batch size has little effect on the training–test accuracy gap.

record.problems: The batch-size gap comparison is described as approximately equivalent without exact values in the supplied text. The dropout comparison is figure-only in the supplied text and its exact accuracy values are not stated. The Imagenet curves mentioned elsewhere average only two runs, but they do not bear on the extracted versions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results were omitted. The adaptive-optimizer comparisons and learning-rate/Hessian estimates do not measure the mapped outcomes for V4 or V7.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label generalization.
Width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under the specified tuning conditions; failure to achieve super-convergence does not establish this comparison.
Batch-size effects with epochs held fixed, including whether recipe adaptation removes a penalty under that budget.
Very small training sets, excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its correlation with generalization gaps, and ranking against norm and margin measures.
Removal of memorized examples compared with random removal and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: No original-source exclusion applies. Table 7 supports better accuracy for larger batches over the tested iteration-based schedule, but does not justify the record's V5 challenges verdict. The supplied text contains no additional qualifying result requiring a missing row.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and generalization on natural labels.
Convolutional versus fully connected image networks.
The mapped comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD or momentum SGD on held-out performance under limited tuning; the paper's optimizer comparisons do not report that comparison.
Fixed-epoch comparisons across image classifiers and language models, and the effects of longer training, warmup, learning-rate scaling, normalization, or other recipe changes.
Whether dropout fails on very small training sets or underfits when too strong; whether removing dropout and weight decay together with augmentation preserves performance.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations and comparisons against norm- and margin-based generalization measures.

rows.check: The 92.1% value is correct, but equal iteration counts give larger batches more training-example presentations. This cannot show reversal under a fixed epoch budget. The note also overlooks the higher 92.4% accuracy at batch size 1000.
